message:
docs(update): the design still said the client comes back through the shell

It is the fallback now, not the route. The primary one duplicates the
shell's token and calls CreateProcessWithTokenW, and the difference that
matters is not the integrity level -- both give Medium -- but that one
hands back a handle and the other does not. A new section says why that
matters: a rollback has to stop what it started before it can move the
files those processes hold, and stopping requires knowing which process
it is. The snapshot comparison that used to answer that question is
recorded there as wrong, beside the answer that replaced it.

Two rows of the state table were also out of date. Relaunch failing is
not uniformly "report, do not roll back" -- that holds for the client and
not for the host or the service, and a check that cannot answer is not
counted as success. Health is asked before any commit, including when an
optional image did not come back, because CreateProcess returning is not
the host being up.

The checklist could not have been followed as written: it asked for an
integrity level, which no longer distinguishes the two routes. It now
says which log line to read, and that an elevated updater falling back
routinely is itself the defect.

Also: the design referenced the ledger by line number, and the line had
already moved. Referencing a growing document by line is a citation with
a short shelf life; both are by ID now.

And the harness still carried the header of the cleanup that was removed
for deleting outside the repository -- including "scoped to this test's
own name pattern, so it can never remove anything else", which is the
reasoning that made it look acceptable in the first place.
